cells.title: Give agents the hub fetch tool and name it in the principle header
cells.action: Add one pub(crate) helper in skillstation_group.rs, `principles_on_hub(root: &Path) -> bool`, true only when the merged config (.bee/config.json overlaid by .bee/config.local.json, through the existing config merge helper) sets `skillstation.principles` to the string `hub`; any other value or absence is false (D1, D5). D5: in principles.rs, when the helper is true for `root`, `principle_lines` appends to the header line the sentence ` Load each one with the skillstation MCP tool skill_get, the slug as skill_id.` (exact text); rows are unchanged, and with the helper false the output is byte-identical to today. D4: the rendered Claude agent file gets `, mcp__skillstation__skill_get` appended to its frontmatter `tools:` line when the helper is true for the repo root; change `render_claude_agent_file` to take the repo root (or a bool) and update both callers, `compute_agent_file_plan` in agents.rs and the `sync_agent_file` arm in apply.rs (around line 870), so plan and apply render the same bytes. A template with no `tools:` line is left as is. With the helper false every rendered agent file is byte-identical to today. Tests: helper true/false/absent/local-overlay cases; header line with and without hub; agent file with and without hub; a re-plan after apply in hub mode carries no sync_agent_file item.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- principles agents skillstation session_preamble

truths: with skillstation.principles set to hub the principle header line names the skillstation MCP tool skill_get
with skillstation.principles absent the principle lines are byte-identical to before
with skillstation.principles set to hub every rendered Claude agent tools line ends with mcp__skillstation__skill_get
with skillstation.principles absent every rendered Claude agent file is byte-identical to before
key_links: principles.rs and agents.rs both call principles_on_hub, not a copy of the config read
plan and apply render agent files through the same function
prohibitions: No change to the agent templates under packages/bee/agents
open_choices: Whether render_claude_agent_file takes the root or a bool

cells.title: Serve principles from the hub in onboard
cells.action: D2: when `principles_on_hub(repo_root)` is true and the Claude runtime is in scope, onboard reads each `bee-principle-*` directory of the engine skills source on the hub with `hub_show` through `hub_runner(repo_root)`. When every one is `active`, the skill sync for the repo Claude target only (target kind repo-claude, `.claude/skills`) leaves every `bee-principle-*` entry out of its source list, so the existing deletion loop plans `remove_skill` for local copies. Codex, opencode, plugin and the legacy global targets are unchanged. When any principle is missing or not active, or the hub read skips, the source list is unchanged and onboard reports exactly one `skipped_skills` entry `{target: "skillstation-principles", reason}` naming the first failing id or the skip reason. D3: when `opts.skillstation` and hub mode, plan one `publish_skillstation` item per `bee-principle-*` source skill that stages from the engine source rendered for the claude runtime (the same render the Claude sync uses), not from `.claude/skills`; apply runs the existing commit-then-activate path. Without hub mode, plan and apply output are byte-identical to today; without --skillstation the hub is never written. Tests use `set_test_hub`, never the real binary: hub mode with all active plans removal of local principle folders only under .claude/skills and keeps .agents copies; one draft keeps all and gives one skip row; hub skip gives one skip row; --skillstation in hub mode plans one publish item per principle; key absent leaves the plan unchanged; a re-plan after apply in hub mode with all active is up to date.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- skillstation onboard

truths: in hub mode with every principle active on the hub onboard removes the local bee-principle folders under .claude/skills only
in hub mode with one principle not active onboard keeps every local principle and reports one skipped_skills entry with target skillstation-principles
bee onboard --skillstation in hub mode publishes each bee-principle skill from the engine source
with skillstation.principles absent the onboard plan is unchanged

cells.action: Document the key: docs/config-reference.md gets `skillstation.principles` (values local and hub, default local, Claude Code only, two onboards to switch). README.md § Skillstation gets one short paragraph. Extend docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/skillstation-hub-skills-and-aliases.md with a section on hub-served principles (D1-D5) and add one line to the Principle homes section of router-triage-and-the-agents-md-duplication-boundary.md pointing at it (one fact, one home). Cite `skillstation-principles D<n>`, never raw decision ids. Run `bee knowledge consolidate --feature skillstation-principles`, write docs/history/skillstation-principles/delivery.md, run `.bee/bin/bee knowledge check` green. One commit.

truths: docs/config-reference.md names skillstation.principles with its two values
the skillstation onboarding concept explains hub-served principles

cells.title: Keep local principles where orient cannot name them
cells.action: D7: in onboard plan, hub mode drops the local principles only when the repo root holds the file principles::PRINCIPLE_INDEX (make the constant reachable from onboard, pub(crate) is enough; do not copy the path string). Check this before the hub read: when the file is absent, principles_from_hub stays false, no hub read runs for principles, and onboard adds exactly one skipped_skills entry {target: "skillstation-principles", reason: "<PRINCIPLE_INDEX> is absent, so bee orient cannot name principles in this repo"}. When the file is present the ssp-2 behavior is unchanged. The --skillstation publish is unchanged. Update the existing ssp-2 hub-mode tests so their repo carries the index file, and add a test: hub mode, every principle active, no index file -> no remove_skill for any bee-principle folder and one skip row naming the index. Docs: say in docs/config-reference.md (the skillstation.principles row), README.md (the Skillstation paragraph; also fix its count: the source has 24 bee-principle skills, not 25) and the onboarding concept that the local copies are removed only in a repo that holds the principle index, which today is the bee repo itself; cite skillstation-principles D7. One commit.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- skillstation onboard

truths: in hub mode with every principle active but no principle index file onboard keeps every local principle and reports one skipped_skills entry naming the index
in hub mode with the principle index file and every principle active onboard still removes the local principle folders under .claude/skills
